xmldoc.short_description: Read or write a MIT-format WFDB annotation file.

param_input_item.param_description: the annotation file (name.atr and the like).
the sampling rate in hertz; when omitted it is taken from a sibling name.hea on disk, or left at one sample per second.
an annotation struct to write; given, the file is written rather than read.

param_output_item.param_description: the annotation struct: column vectors of sample, time, code, symbol, num, subtype, chan and aux.

description.p: Reads a MIT-format annotation file into the module's annotation struct, and with a struct as the second argument writes one back, so that a read followed by a write and a read returns it unchanged.

Each annotation is a sixteen-bit word, least significant byte first: the top six bits are the code and the low ten are the samples since the last mark. Five codes are not marks but instructions: a code of 59 carries a long gap in the two words after it as a signed thirty-two-bit number, 60 sets the num, 61 the subtype of the next mark, 62 the channel, and 63 introduces a text that names the mark; a zero word ends the file. The sample index is rebuilt from the running gap, and the code of each mark is mapped to its PhysioNet mnemonic in symbol.

The sample index is what the file stores; the time in seconds is (sample - 1) / rate, so the rate is needed only to place the marks in time and is taken from the record's header when a sibling name.hea is beside the file.

xmldoc.bibliography: Goldberger et al., PhysioBank, PhysioToolkit, and PhysioNet, Circulation 101(23), 2000; Moody and Mark, The impact of the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology 20(3), 2001.
